lead: An optical amplifier boosts light directly, without converting it to electrons. A pump feeds energy into a gain medium, and signal photons trigger stimulated emission that copies them. Before amplifiers, every span ended at a receiver and a fresh transmitter; now one amplifier per span lifts every WDM channel at once. Only a few syllabi teach amplifiers in this depth. EDFAs serve 1550 nm long-haul links; SOAs serve shorter and cheaper links.
prereq: You need: stimulated emission and population inversion (see Absorption, spontaneous and stimulated emission), dBm power units, and the WDM coupler and isolator (Passive devices).

sections.h3: Why amplify, and the five numbers

blocks.text: Fiber at 1550 nm loses about 0.2 dB per km, so an 80 km span loses 16 dB and eight spans 128 dB, far beyond any power budget. An amplifier after each span restores the power, and the same light continues.

G is the gain; P<sub>out</sub> and P<sub>in</sub> are the signal powers out and in, in the same unit. In dBm, P<sub>out</sub>(dBm) = P<sub>in</sub>(dBm) + G(dB); a 20 dB gain means P<sub>out</sub> = 100 × P<sub>in</sub>.
Five numbers appear on every amplifier data sheet.

items: Gain: 20 to 40 dB; it sets how much span loss one amplifier can pay back.
Gain bandwidth: the wavelength range where the gain stays within a stated drop; the EDFA C-band is about 35 nm wide.
Saturation output power: the output at which the gain has fallen by 3 dB from its small-signal value.
Noise figure NF = 10 log₁₀(SNR<sub>in</sub>/SNR<sub>out</sub>): the SNR lost in the amplifier; about 3 dB is the limit for a high-gain amplifier, and lower is better.
Polarization dependence: the gain difference between input polarizations, in dB; large in plain SOAs and small in EDFAs.

blocks.text: A semiconductor optical amplifier (SOA) is a laser diode chip driven by current but stopped from lasing. Anti-reflection coatings on both facets remove the feedback, so light passes once through the active region and is amplified by stimulated emission. Different material compositions cover 1310 nm and 1550 nm. Gain is 20 to 30 dB and the noise figure is usually 6 to 9 dB.

Two weaknesses limit its use. The gain depends on polarization, often by several dB, because the active region is thin and flat. And the carrier lifetime is below a nanosecond, so a strong channel modulates the gain seen by its neighbours: cross-gain modulation, a crosstalk between WDM channels (WDM concepts). The same fast response makes SOAs useful as gates and wavelength converters, and as cheap boosters in short links.

An EDFA is a length of silica fiber, typically 10 to 30 m, whose core is doped with Er³⁺ ions. A 980 nm pump photon lifts an ion from the ground level 1 to level 3, which decays within microseconds to the metastable level 2 (lifetime about 10 ms). A signal photon near 1550 nm then stimulates the 2 → 1 transition and gains an identical copy. A 1480 nm pump lifts ions straight into the top of level 2. The 980 nm pump gives the more complete inversion and so the lower noise figure; the 1480 nm pump gives more output power per pump watt.

The parts in signal order are an input isolator, a WDM coupler that merges pump and signal, the doped fiber, an output isolator and a gain-flattening filter. The isolators stop reflections and backward amplified spontaneous emission (ASE) from turning the amplifier into a laser. The C-band runs from 1530 to 1565 nm with 20 to 40 dB gain and NF of 4 to 6 dB; a longer doped fiber gives gain in the L-band, 1570 to 1610 nm.

Energy conservation caps the output. Each pump photon can make at most one signal photon, and a signal photon carries less energy (E = hc/λ). So the added signal power can be at most (λ<sub>p</sub>/λ<sub>s</sub>) times the pump power:

PCE is the power conversion efficiency; P<sub>s,out</sub> and P<sub>s,in</sub> are the signal powers out and in; P<sub>p</sub> is the pump power. The limit is PCE ≤ λ<sub>p</sub>/λ<sub>s</sub>, which is 980/1550 = 0.632 for a 980 nm pump. The quantum conversion efficiency QCE = PCE × λ<sub>s</sub>/λ<sub>p</sub> is the share of pump photons turned into signal photons, at most 1.

Each amplifier in a chain adds ASE noise. For N identical spans the optical signal-to-noise ratio in 0.1 nm at 1550 nm is about OSNR(dB) = 58 + P<sub>in</sub>(dBm) − NF(dB) − 10 log₁₀ N, where P<sub>in</sub> is the power of one channel at each amplifier input and 58 dB comes from the photon energy and the 0.1 nm bandwidth. Noise adds up, so OSNR falls by 10 log₁₀ N: eight amplifiers cost 9.03 dB. Raman amplification, which pumps the transmission fiber itself, is covered with Nonlinear scattering: stimulated Brillouin and Raman.

examples.question: A 10 Gb/s channel is launched into a chain of 8 spans. Each span loses 20 dB and is followed by an EDFA with 20 dB gain and a noise figure of 5 dB. The power into the first amplifier is −20 dBm. (a) Show that every amplifier sees the same input. (b) Estimate the OSNR after the last amplifier with OSNR = 58 + P<sub>in</sub> − NF − 10 log₁₀ N.
steps: Each span takes away 20 dB and each amplifier gives back 20 dB, so the net change per span is 0 dB. Amplifier 1 sees −20 dBm and puts out 0 dBm; span 2 brings it back to −20 dBm, and so on. Every amplifier input is −20 dBm.
Check: one amplifier alone would give 58 − 20 − 5 = 33 dB, and 33 − 9.03 = 23.97 dB.
examples.answer: Every amplifier input is −20 dBm, and the OSNR after 8 spans is about 24.0 dB, of which 9.03 dB is lost to noise accumulation.

examples.question: An EDFA is pumped with 60 mW at 980 nm. A 1550 nm signal of 0.5 mW goes in and 25 mW comes out. Find (a) the gain in dB, (b) the power conversion efficiency, (c) the quantum conversion efficiency, and (d) the largest output and gain energy conservation allows with this pump.
steps: (c) QCE = PCE × λ<sub>s</sub>/λ<sub>p</sub> = 0.408 × 1550/980 = 0.408 × 1.582 = 0.646, so 64.6 percent of the pump photons become signal photons.

(d) Limit: P<sub>s,out</sub> ≤ P<sub>s,in</sub> + (λ<sub>p</sub>/λ<sub>s</sub>)P<sub>p</sub> = 0.5 + 0.632 × 60 = 0.5 + 37.94 = 38.44 mW. Maximum gain = 10 log₁₀(38.44/0.5) = 10 log₁₀ 76.9 = 18.86 dB.
Check: the measured 25 mW is below the 38.44 mW limit, and the QCE is below 1, as it must be.
examples.answer: G = 16.99 dB, PCE = 40.8 percent, QCE = 64.6 percent; at most 38.44 mW out, a gain of 18.86 dB.

traps: An amplifier is not a regenerator: it restores power but not pulse shape, so dispersion and jitter pass straight through.
Noise adds up: N identical amplifiers lower the OSNR by 10 log₁₀ N, so 8 amplifiers cost 9.03 dB, not 8 times one amplifier’s penalty.
PCE cannot reach 100 percent: with a 980 nm pump and a 1550 nm signal the ceiling is 980/1550 = 63.2 percent, because each signal photon carries less energy than a pump photon.
The EDFA C-band is 1530 to 1565 nm, not the whole low-loss window from 1260 to 1625 nm.
An SOA facet without its anti-reflection coating gives feedback, and the chip lases instead of amplifying.

quiz.q: Define gain in dB for an optical amplifier.
quiz.a: G(dB) = 10 log₁₀(P<sub>out</sub>/P<sub>in</sub>); 20 dB means P<sub>out</sub> = 100 P<sub>in</sub>.

quiz.q: Name the two common EDFA pump wavelengths and the C-band range.
quiz.a: 980 nm and 1480 nm; the C-band is about 1530 to 1565 nm.

quiz.q: Why is the noise figure of a 980 nm pumped EDFA lower than that of an SOA?
quiz.a: Noise figure depends on how complete the population inversion is. A 980 nm pump empties the ground level almost completely, so few ions absorb and the spontaneous-emission factor is close to 1, giving NF near 4 dB. An SOA has incomplete inversion and higher internal and coupling losses, giving 6 to 9 dB.

quiz.q: P<sub>in</sub> = −22 dBm, NF = 6 dB, N = 4 amplifiers. Estimate the OSNR in 0.1 nm at 1550 nm.
A 1480 nm pump of 60 mW drives an EDFA with 0.5 mW of 1550 nm input. What is the largest possible signal output?
quiz.a: P<sub>s,out</sub> ≤ 0.5 + (1480/1550) × 60 = 0.5 + 0.955 × 60 = 57.79 mW, more than the 38.44 mW allowed with a 980 nm pump of the same power.

quiz.q: By how much does the OSNR fall when a chain grows from 1 to 16 identical amplifiers, and what does that suggest for long links?
quiz.a: 10 log₁₀ 16 = 12.04 dB. Each doubling of the chain costs 3.01 dB, so long links need low-NF amplifiers, high input power per channel, or shorter spans.

beyond: Not for the exam. Long-haul systems combine EDFAs with Raman pumping and dynamic gain equalisation. Research pushes the L-band, few-mode erbium-doped fiber and erbium-doped waveguide amplifiers on silicon photonics. Search for gain flattening and erbium-doped waveguide amplifier.

figure.caption: Top: a 0.5 mW signal passes an isolator, joins a 60 mW 980 nm pump in the WDM coupler, is amplified in the doped fiber and leaves through a second isolator and the gain-flattening filter at 25 mW, a gain of 16.99 dB and a PCE of 40.8 percent. Bottom: the 980 nm pump lifts ions to level 3, they fall quickly to the long-lived level 2, and the signal stimulates the 2 → 1 transition.
